newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Bomb explosion in Nigerian capital wounds eight.
newsitem.headline: Bomb explosion in Nigerian capital wounds eight.

text.p: A bomb exploded when a military bus was passing in a street in the Nigerian capital on Wednesday, wounding eight people, Lagos state police chief said.
"The blast went off when the military bus was passing," police commissioner Abubakar Tsav told Reuters. "Five of the people injured are military including a female soldier."
"Bomb disposal experts have recovered the device in today's explosion and it is similar to the ones used in previous attacks," Tsav said.
It was the fourth blast in Lagos since December. A bomb hit an army bus in Lagos in January killing three soldiers and wounding dozens of others.
In December, two bombs exploded within days targeting the military administrator of Lagos state Colonel Muhammed Marwa, a close aide of military ruler General Sani Abacha.
The police blame the opposition NADECO group for the string of explosions in politically volatile Nigeria and have detained 22 persons over the blasts. NADECO denies any involvement.
